question_type: Mean of 120 monthly spreads (Aa new corporate minus long-term Treasury) from one pinned issue's Table AY-1, a 4-column-group x 3-stacked-year layout whose year-label rows were lost in OCR; 5 significant digits
decisive_step: Assigning the right calendar year to each of the 36 monthly rows x 4 column groups of Table AY-1 in treasury_bulletin_1970_06.txt:4946-4984 (the year labels are not in the text). The right mapping is group1 = the year before the range and the first two years of the range, groups 2-3 = the next three-year runs, group4 = the last two years of the range plus the publication year (partially filled). Off by one block = averages 1959-1968 (~12% low). The reference anchored the mapping from the same table in the May and July 1970 printings (worklog Step 3; treasury_bulletin_1970_05.txt:4847,4862,4875) and cross-checked all 240 cells against May (worklog Step 4). Vintage is pinned by the question (June 1970), and every cell was right to use June values.

a.path_summary: find_tables took four tries (a[5] zero hits for the question's noun phrase, a[7] output cut at 8000 bytes, a[9]/a[11] narrowed to 1970) to land on AY-1 in the June 1970 issue. show_table --long --grep 196 at a[14] matched only the four weekly Dec-1969 rows (the monthly rows carry no year), so it fell back to sed on the raw file (a[16] failed with a relative path, a[18] worked) and looked at the July 1970 printing raw (a[28], a[39]) to infer the year blocks. Three calc attempts: a[33]/a[35] parsed only the first column group (36 months), a[41] mapped group 1 to the first year of the range (off by one block, which it caught because the count came out 132 instead of 120), a[43] used the right offsets and produced 120 months.

first_divergence.what_it_did: Correct mapping and mean over 120 months; the 5-significant-digit value was exact.

b.path_summary: Found the June 1970 table by rg at b[14]-[16] and noticed at b[17] that the year headers were missing. It then convinced itself the table covered only the last few years (b[50], b[54]) and searched the issue for a separate 1960-69 series, repeating one rg command 139 times (b[70]-b[346], every run identical) until a context compaction. After compaction (b[347]) it used find_tables and show_table --stitch (b[351]-[358]), which showed the four panels with YEAR_UNKNOWN flags and the sibling list; it first guessed the panels one year too early (b[359], b[364]), then at b[376] re-anchored by counting the partial last panel back from the publication month, and computed the 120-month mean at b[377]. The submit gate (b[380]) asked it to anchor the Y? rows from a sibling; it read the July 1970 raw table at b[387], confirmed the mapping, and kept the same answer (b[389], b[393]).

smallest_change.change: show_table already detects rows without a printed year (Y?/YEAR_UNKNOWN) and lists SIBLINGS, but leaves the anchoring to the model. Make it do the anchoring: when a table has YEAR_UNKNOWN rows and a sibling printing of the same table id and width (same or adjacent calendar year, nearest issue first) has year labels, align the two by exact cell agreement of one full row block per panel and print, in NOTES and in the period column: 'YEARS ANCHORED from treasury_bulletin_1970_05.txt:4843 (240/240 cells agree): panel1 = 1959,1960,1961; panel2 = 1962,1963,1964; panel3 = 1965,1966,1967; panel4 = 1968,1969,1970 (partial, ends 1970-05)'. Rows then read '1960-01' instead of 'Y?-01', tagged '<anchored>' rather than YEAR_UNKNOWN. If no sibling aligns, print 'no sibling aligns - years unknown' and keep Y?. Add a feasibility line: 'last filled month 1970-05 is consistent with issue 1970_06'. Also make --stitch/--cols the default view for multi-panel tables so 36 rows x 4 panels fit one 8000-byte page instead of 28 virtual rows (c[26], b[355]-[358]).
would_have_fixed: none wrong here; it would have removed the year-inference detour in all three cells (a[19]-[42], b[359]-[376] and gate round 1, c[27]-[39]) and it is exactly the fix for the v8 cards failure on this question (one-year block shift)
smallest_change.could_hurt_right_cells: unlikely - the anchoring is printed only when a sibling matches cell-for-cell; a wrong anchor cannot pass that test, and the raw labels stay visible

alternatives.change: Loop guard escalation: after the note at the threshold, if the same command (identical output sha) is issued again, replace its output with one line '[harness] identical output to call N suppressed (k repeats); run a different command or submit' instead of re-inserting 8 KB, and after 3 more repeats force a compaction whose summary lists the commands already tried. In b this would have cut ~130 wasted requests and ~20 M input tokens.
alternatives.why_not_first: It fixes cost, not correctness; b was right in the end. But the current guard fires once per command (controller_runtime.py _loop_guard: 'if cmd in self.noted: continue') and then lets the model repeat the command 136 more times, which is the single largest operational cost in this pilot's cell b.

alternatives.change: Add to the table notes: 'If show_table marks rows Y? (year not printed), open the sibling printing it lists (show_table <sibling> --cols 1-6) and read the years from there; a partially filled last panel ends at the issue's publication month.'
alternatives.why_not_first: All three cells got there without it, and the v8 cards arm shows that text-guided anchoring from the wrong sibling (next calendar year) still fails; the tool can verify the alignment, the text cannot.

alternatives.change: find_tables: stem tokens (bond/bonds, yield/yields) and fall back to any-token OR ranking when the AND query returns 0, printing 'no table has all words; best partial matches:' so a[5], c[4], c[12] would have listed AY-1 immediately.
alternatives.why_not_first: Cost only (2-6 wasted calls per cell); every cell found the table.

fix.why_not_text: Cell a had the text and still needed nine raw-file/sed steps and three calc iterations to recover the years; the text cannot tell the model which of two candidate block mappings is right, whereas a tool that prints the anchored years with a cell-agreement count settles it in one output. The v8 cards arm applied 'anchor from another printing' with a rolled-forward next-year printing and got the off-by-one answer.
fix.irreducible: no - the question is unambiguous once the years are anchored; all cells were right

notes: Three observations for v10. (1) show_table --long --grep <year> is a trap on tables whose monthly rows have no printed year: a[14] got 'page rows 1-4 of 4' (only weekly rows with a 1969 date) and concluded the tool view was broken. (2) The gate rule 'Y? row -> anchor with a sibling' worked as designed in b (it prompted the July 1970 check) but the second finding ('uses line 4985, a value no tool output showed') was a false positive from the calc line-range end; the rule should skip lines that hold no numeric cell. (3) The compaction summary in b carried a wrong structural belief ('table covers only 1967-70') that the model had to overturn; a ledger line recording the table's row/column shape (36 month rows x 4 panels, YEAR_UNKNOWN, siblings) would be a safer splice than free-text summary. The reference's extra safety step - cross-checking every cell against the sibling printing - is cheap to fold into the same tool change. The v8 per-question analysis (018.json) lists the same TOOL remedy ('find labeled printings of this table, nearest same-year first') and a cross-vintage alignment CHECK.
